title: Describe deforming motifs by their responses, not their silhouettes
hypothesis: Response descriptors may distinguish visually similar motifs with different load transfer, while visual descriptors may separate silhouettes that implement nearly identical responses.
experiment: On CPU, sample 100 twelve-node motifs and solve fixed-boundary linear equilibria. Build equal-size response and silhouette archives from the identical pool; evaluate withheld load directions.
falsifier: Reject the proposed advantage if held-out response separation is no better than random across repeated pools, or follows only node count or stiffness totals.

title: Compile relation graphs into a bounded Lenia kernel grammar
hypothesis: If reusable motifs provide useful search structure, grammar mutations may retain viable patterns more often than matched flat mutations after a new channel coupling is introduced.
experiment: Run 60 paired mutations on a 32-by-32 grid for 150 steps, matching starting patterns and parameter ranges; evaluate a withheld seed.
falsifier: Reject a grammar benefit if matched flat encoding performs equally or better, or any apparent gain disappears after matching the distribution of coefficient changes.

title: Test when nonreciprocal particle couplings produce functional pursuit
hypothesis: Under specified drag and resource attraction, asymmetric coefficients may support sustained pursuit with better tracking than reciprocal couplings of the same interaction strength.
experiment: Simulate 24 particles for 400 steps over 40 coefficient pairs and ten seeds; displace a resource halfway through and measure tracking after the intervention.
falsifier: Reject the pursuit claim if tracking gains vanish under matched force magnitude or occur equally when the resource displacement signal is removed.

title: Couple elastic deformation to a local reaction pattern
hypothesis: Within a stable parameter region, two-way coupling may preserve a traveling excitation after a localized mechanical disturbance more often than one-way coupling.
experiment: Sweep 30 coupling settings, ten seeds and 500 steps; indent one ring node at a fixed time and track pulse propagation and recovery with timestep-halving checks.
falsifier: Reject the coupling advantage if it disappears under timestep refinement or if comparable persistence requires no strain feedback.

title: Give a spring motif a local record of previous loading
hypothesis: A slow internal variable may preserve information about pulse order after fast displacement relaxes, permitting better discrimination than a memoryless spring motif.
experiment: Apply AB and BA load pulses with equal total impulse; after a fixed delay, apply the same probe and classify histories using displacement in 100 noisy repeats.
falsifier: Reject hidden-memory behavior if classification falls to chance after geometry matching, or if initial-state leakage predicts history equally well.

title: Separate refractory-state memory from visible cellular shape
hypothesis: If refractory state stores operational history, identical visible patterns should respond differently to an identical probe after h swapping, with differences decaying at the specified relaxation timescale.
experiment: Use 32-by-32 grids, paired activation pulses and ten seeds; copy visible state across matched histories, then swap hidden channels before applying a fixed probe.
falsifier: Reject a refractory-memory explanation if hidden-state swaps do not alter response, or differences persist unchanged after resetting h.

title: Select locally persistent patterns for recovery across lesion types
hypothesis: At equal rollout budget, lesion-conditioned selection may improve recovery to withheld lesion locations compared with selection for undisturbed persistence alone.
experiment: Mutate 80 candidates around a known viable seed on a 32-by-32 grid. Alternate two training lesion classes; evaluate retained patterns on held-out wedge lesions and seeds.
falsifier: Reject transferable recovery if gains occur only for trained lesion masks, reflect simply larger initial mass, or disappear on held-out initial conditions.

title: Select visual novelty against intervention-tested function
hypothesis: Function-conditioned selection may resist color-cycle novelty traps better than visual selection while retaining patterns with distinct responses to local deletion and timed excitation.
experiment: Evaluate 80 shared candidate rules on 24-by-24 grids with three renderers; build equal-capacity archives and evaluate unselected perturbation times and deletion locations.
falsifier: Reject the selection advantage if response-selected archives lack more held-out functional diversity than random or are equally altered by renderer-only changes.

title: Typed evidence packets for collective hidden-state inference
hypothesis: Typed packets should reduce error more under duplicated reports than independent reports, specifically testing resistance to repeated hearsay.
experiment: Vary duplication and sensor reliability in matched CPU runs; fix sensor draws, packet capacity and total messages across formats.
falsifier: Reject if untyped packets with identical provenance match accuracy, or gains require greater packet capacity or more sensor samples.

title: Collective descriptors that separate coordination from shared drift
hypothesis: Graph descriptors should retain more transfer strategies succeeding after spatial shifts; image descriptors should retain more shifted duplicates.
experiment: Compare matched descriptor archives in grid-world populations, then replay frozen elites on translated and shuffled-resource maps with identical budgets.
falsifier: Reject if image elites match after translated duplicates merge, or graph descriptors erase spatial specialization needed for resource delivery.

title: Contradiction-triggered quorum checks in communicating populations
hypothesis: Contradiction-triggered sampling should reduce false alarms under localized failures, but lose its advantage under common-mode corruption shared by all sensors.
experiment: Replay matched sensor draws under localized and shared failures; equalize sampling budgets across challenge, broadcast and independent conditions.
falsifier: Reject if random resampling matches targeted challenges, or if gains disappear after extra sensor observations and messages are equalized.

title: Novelty-guided communication routing through complementary sensors
hypothesis: Source-combination routing should improve parity recovery on sparse networks; gains should shrink when every component is already directly accessible.
experiment: Evolve route policies across small graphs; test held-out sensor allocations and edge failures using matched puzzles and packet budgets.
falsifier: Reject if source-aware random routing matches accuracy, or gains depend on withholding equivalent information from the independent ensemble reducer.

title: A minority-memory archive for collective adaptation after regime shifts
hypothesis: Minority-policy memory should shorten recovery after recurring regime shifts, while producing a measurable stationary-environment cost from reserving archive space.
experiment: Run recurring, unprecedented and absent regime shifts in matched grid-world seeds; equalize memory slots, retrieval attempts and simulator steps.
falsifier: Reject if reward-only retention matches recovery under equal memory, or benefits occur only on previously memorized resource layouts.

title: Provenance memory that limits collective error cascades
hypothesis: Ancestry memory should accelerate correction after influential-source failure, particularly in clustered networks that repeatedly circulate the same observation.
experiment: Replay binary reports through graph populations; time a ground-truth correction and vary clustering while matching packets, memory and sensor reliability.
falsifier: Reject if flat source-tagged memory matches ancestry tracking, or if ancestry discounting suppresses genuinely independent corroboration enough to negate gains.

title: Selecting complementary role mixtures instead of individually strong agents
hypothesis: Team niche selection should retain useful signalers under sparse discovery; their advantage should diminish when all resources become directly visible.
experiment: Evolve finite-state teams under sparse visibility, then test dense visibility and role removal with matched mutation opportunities and simulator evaluations.
falsifier: Reject complementarity if removing signalers changes no reward, or if matched reward-only selection finds equally effective teams at equal budget.

title: Selecting collective policies across communication breakdown niches
hypothesis: Niche-selected mixtures should recover consensus after communication-regime switches more reliably than average-reward selection, while causing errors near switching boundaries.
experiment: Train on separate packet-fault regimes, then test held-out switching sequences; equalize evaluations, messages and network-detector information across conditions.
falsifier: Reject if detector-equipped homogeneous policies match recovery, or mixed populations succeed only by transmitting additional packets during regime transitions.

title: Behavioral niches for evidence-retrieval workflows
hypothesis: Behavioral niches preserve retrieval strategies useful for different test materials questions, improving worst-question-type performance compared with selecting one globally highest-scoring retriever.
experiment: Author fifty evidence cards with explicit claims and distractors. Split templates before searching retrieval depth, relation filters and contradiction rules; freeze workflows before testing.
falsifier: Reject the advantage if worst-template accuracy fails to improve across matched seeds, or if randomly permuted descriptors perform equally well at equal budgets.

title: Counterfactual descriptors for graph-guided experiment plans
hypothesis: Counterfactual descriptors retain experiments discriminating different mechanisms, whereas lexical novelty retains differently phrased plans with redundant consequences on test model pairs.
experiment: Author three spring-network laws and candidate measures. Archive graph-derived plans on training networks, then test frozen selections on withheld networks and hidden laws.
falsifier: Reject the proposal if discrimination niches do not improve identification or reduce redundancy, or gains disappear when every method receives identical initial plans.

title: Compatibility-tested recombination of scientific workflows
hypothesis: Compatibility-constrained recombination yields more accurate executable workflows per evaluation than unconstrained crossover; factorial tests reveal individually useful modules that become harmful together.
experiment: Build spring-network tasks and typed modules containing unit and boundary-condition traps. Search training topologies, then execute selected workflows on unseen topology families.
falsifier: Reject synergy if one substitution explains child improvements, or screening gives no advantage beyond syntax filtering at matched total evaluation costs.

title: Evidence-coupled competition among experiment plans
hypothesis: Evidence-coupled updates avoid duplicated experiments and preserve alternative explanations longer than independent rankings, improving hidden-model identification within a fixed total measure budget.
experiment: Simulate noisy measures from competing spring laws. Tune plan-update rules on training cases; evaluate frozen policies with new noise seeds and withheld parameters.
falsifier: Reject the mechanism if gains persist after shared-evidence randomization, or vanish when equivalent duplicate-removal bookkeeping is supplied to every control at matched cost.

title: A failure archive that redirects graph exploration
hypothesis: Negative-result memory reduces invalid repetition and discovers more distinct valid experiment plans per evaluation budget than retaining successful hypotheses alone.
experiment: Construct graphs with hidden unit, incompatibility and unsupported-edge traps. Reveal failures only upon evaluation; test test instances sharing failure categories but different paths.
falsifier: Reject added value if exact-path deduplication matches performance, or if improvements require hidden constraint labels leaking into unevaluated paths through archive features.

title: Lineage-preserving reuse of experiment subroutines
hypothesis: Diverse reusable libraries reduce solver calls on test tasks; lineage and assumption checks prevent inappropriate transfers between cases that share superficial descriptions.
experiment: Create stiffness-estimation, boundary-checking and identifiability tasks. Populate memory on training topology families, then assemble validated workflows for withheld families within fixed execution budgets.
falsifier: Reject the advantage if matching library size and provenance removes benefits, or rare routine retention increases coverage without improving test accuracy or efficiency.

title: Local competition across experiment-cost niches
hypothesis: Cost-conditioned archives improve correct-model identification across test budgets because inexpensive useful plans survive despite having lower absolute info scores than expensive alternatives.
experiment: Define noisy spring measures with explicit costs. Search training models, then evaluate archive retrieval on withheld models at prespecified small, medium and large budgets.
falsifier: Reject added benefit if Pareto retention matches every budget result at equivalent storage and scoring costs, or if gains require post-hoc budget bins.

title: Select research directions by novelty that survives re-description
hypothesis: Consequence-constrained novelty retains more informative experiments and fewer paraphrase duplicates than single-encoding novelty, while preserving supported-plan quality on unseen questions.
experiment: Author forty directions with known consequences and paraphrases. Tune training thresholds; select equal-sized archives on withheld consequences and separately generated transformations.
falsifier: Reject added value if consequence deduplication matches performance, or invariance filtering merges substantively different plans because relevant contexts escape the encoding.

title: Archive spring motifs with frozen response tests and rank checks
hypothesis: Response selection may preserve more withheld-load variation than silhouettes after rank and material-budget checks; graph guidance may add nothing beyond arbitrary descriptor choice.
experiment: Freeze twenty pools of 100 accepted motifs, with a 200-attempt cap and all rejection counts reported. Training descriptors concatenate free-node displacements under unit x and y loads at the top-right node. Retain twenty motifs by identical farthest-point selection and deterministic ties. Evaluate loads at the middle-right node at angles 45,135,225,315 degrees; no evaluation coordinates enter selection.
falsifier: Reject a useful descriptor advantage if the paired uncertainty includes no improvement over random across pools, or effects vanish after fixed material-budget control. Reject graph-specific benefit if shuffled-path descriptors perform equally.

title: Disentangle asymmetric pursuit from sensing and actuation budgets
hypothesis: Nonreciprocity may improve resource tracking beyond a reciprocal interaction and resource-only controller, conditional on realized actuation work; unequal parameter counts remain a limitation, not a removed difference.
experiment: Run twelve independent searches per family, each evaluating 24 coefficients on three fixed training seeds for 300 steps; resource jumps at step 150. Fix a11=a22=0 and Frobenius norm of off-diagonal coefficients to one. Select by training tracking, then evaluate ten untouched seeds and eight withheld resource jumps/directions, paired across families. Repeat selected tests at dt=0.01 for equal duration.
falsifier: Reject the claimed advantage if it disappears under common-work comparisons, fails withheld jumps, equals resource-only control, survives frozen sensing equally, or changes materially with timestep halving.

title: Test reachable refractory histories and artificial hidden-state swaps
hypothesis: History-dependent responses may persist beyond visible-state matching, with a delay scale related to h decay; spatially organized history must outperform equal-mean and equal-variance controls to support more than scalar excitability.
experiment: Initialize twenty independently jittered disks, h=0. Training pulses add 0.10 inside a radius-two disk at steps 10 and 30; probe adds 0.05 at step 60. Freeze probe response as total x change over the next twenty steps minus a paired no-probe trajectory, normalized by initial mass. Hold out pulse intervals 7,17,37 and delays 10,30,60 steps; record extinction rather than omit it.
falsifier: Reject an operational history effect if resetting h leaves the difference unchanged or effects fail the 0.05 threshold. Reject a spatial-memory claim if shuffled maps match localized maps. If no reachable x-matched pairs exist, restrict conclusions to artificial intervention sensitivity.

title: Freeze renderer traps and held-out functions before archive selection
hypothesis: Response selection may preserve held-out function while resisting color-only novelty. Corrupting response labels should remove any advantage dependent on accurate measurements.
experiment: Freeze twenty seed-specific pools of eighty rules: mu uniform 0.15–0.45, sigma 0.02–0.10, kernel radius 2–5, fixed jittered seed disks, 24-by-24 periodic grids and 200 steps. Viability requires mass in [0.2,3] times initial mass and no more than half the grid above 0.9 at step 200. Train assays at step 100: radius-two erasure at (6,6) and +0.1 pulse at (18,18).
falsifier: Reject a functional advantage if it fails held-out perturbation families or merely selects failures. Reject renderer robustness if membership changes under color-only transformations. If corrupted labels perform equally, reject a measurement-specific benefit.

title: Typed evidence packets tested against correlation and equal-bit controls
hypothesis: Typing should reduce decision error beyond source-ID deduplication only when relation compatibility carries useful information; deduplication alone should address repeated relays but not distinct sensors sharing hidden causes.
experiment: Factorially ablate typing, provenance and uncertainty, with 16 observations and 32 transmitted 64-bit packets per episode. Freeze weights on training worlds. Hold out reliability ranges, duplicate rates and shared-cause generator families; pair methods within independent worlds, not individual packets.
falsifier: Reject an incremental typing benefit if source-tagged flat aggregation matches it after equal encoding, observations and access. Reject provenance-as-independence if distinct correlated sensors still induce overconfidence, even when duplicate relays are perfectly removed.

title: A fixed-budget contradiction protocol with episode-level failure tests
hypothesis: Targeted challenges should improve the error-delay frontier over cyclic or random resampling under localized failures, but their advantage should shrink under episode-wide common-mode corruption despite identical sample schedules.
experiment: Pregenerate per-sensor sample streams; every policy receives eight initial plus eight reserved samples at identical times. Compare allocations using independent failure episodes, reserving spatial and temporal failure-generator families. Primary decisions occur at round four; secondary stopping thresholds use identical permitted times.
falsifier: Reject the interaction benefit if cyclic or random allocation matches its frontier under the same deadlines, observation count and bit ceiling. Report a common-mode failure boundary even if localized cases improve.

title: Claim-specific provenance memory with fallible corrections
hypothesis: Ancestry memory should reduce persistent false consensus beyond source-ID deduplication when relays obscure observation identity, but its advantage should decline as ancestry corruption or correction unreliability increases.
experiment: Replay independent report-cascade episodes with identical correction arrival times. Train then freeze discount rules; test held-out graph families, correction-error generators and ancestry-loss mechanisms. Include false corrections and distinct sources sharing hidden causes, not only duplicated relays.
falsifier: Reject the graph-memory advantage if observation-ID flat memory matches it at equal byte cost. Reject the correction rule if false corrections erase valid corroboration or its gains require privileged true corrections unavailable to controls.

title: Team-level selection with matched-cost role replacement controls
hypothesis: Niche-selected teams should retain signalers whose removal reduces held-out sparse-map deliveries beyond matched-cost replacements. Their contribution should shrink under dense visibility; archive benefits must also exceed reward-only team search at equal evaluation cost.
experiment: Run independent searches with identical training visibility distributions and fixed capacities. Hold out map-generator families, obstacles and resource clustering, including unseen sparse maps and dense controls. Evaluate frozen teams; replace signalers with neutral or alternative-role agents, keeping ten agents and action capacities fixed.
falsifier: Reject signaler complementarity if neutral or alternative-role replacements preserve delivery at matched cost. Reject an archive-specific benefit if reward-only team search reaches equivalent held-out performance and interaction coverage under identical search budgets.

title: Identifiability-audited descriptors for experiment-plan search
hypothesis: Discrimination niches may preserve complementary plans and reduce redundant measurements versus lexical novelty. Incremental value beyond expected-information selection remains an open empirical question, not an assumed advantage.
experiment: Normalized spring laws: F=kx; F=kx+ax^3; F=kx+a max(0,x-x0), positive parameters. Loads {0.1,0.3,0.6,1.0}; displacement noise N(0,0.01^2). Solve parallel-spring networks by bisection. Training calibration freezes priors and rejection thresholds. Reserve topology generators and parameter ranges; test fourth law F=kx+a tanh(x/b), b>0. Build twenty independent archives with paired problem/noise seeds across methods.
falsifier: No support if niches fail to improve preregistered accuracy or redundancy across independent builds. Failure against expected information limits added value. Fourth-law detection is scored only where oracle distinguishability holds; otherwise report non-identifiability.

title: Budget-accounted factorial tests of workflow recombination
hypothesis: Assumption-aware compatibility may improve valid workflows per computational cost. Recombination needs to exceed mutation and type filtering; source papers do not establish workflow-crossover synergy.
experiment: Publish fixed modules and spring generators before search: SI conversion, boundary assembly, linearization and nonlinear bisection. Some modules pass types but violate assumptions. Reserve topology generators and entire assumption-error families. Run twenty independent searches; estimate factorial contrasts within matched withheld problems and noise seeds.
falsifier: Reject added value if assumption checks do not exceed type-only controls at primary cost, or one substitution explains all improvement without negative interaction. Contrasts depend on loss scale, not universal scientific synergy.

title: Exception-aware failure memory without hidden-label access
hypothesis: Failure-context memory may reduce invalid repetition beyond exact deduplication and failure counts without suppressing valid exceptions. Novelty and evidence validity remain separately measured.
experiment: Publish graph generator, deterministic oracle, signature vocabulary and equal feature weights before testing. Oracle labels appear only after charged queries. Include unit mismatch, unsupported edges and context-conditional incompatibility with rule-reversing exceptions. Mark 10% of training feedback uncertain, represented as unknown rather than hard failures. Reserve graphs and context-rule combinations; run thirty independent paired graph/search builds.
falsifier: No added support if deduplication or constraint learning matches valid-plan yield, or novelty suppresses context reversals. Requiring hidden failure labels in candidate features invalidates the run rather than supporting memory.

title: Fair cost-niche selection against budget-aware Pareto archives
hypothesis: Cost niches may improve budget-conditioned accuracy over global top-k. Incremental benefit over same-capacity Pareto retention is separate; equal Pareto performance does not invalidate meaningful cost-conditioned coverage.
experiment: Use F=kx, F=kx+ax^3 and F=kx+a max(0,x-x0), positive parameters; displacement noise N(0,0.01^2); finite load plans from {0.1,0.3,0.6,1}. Cost sums public measurement costs; training accuracy and discrimination determine retention. Reserve topology generators, parameters and noise. Build thirty independent paired archives with the same pools and seeds. Test budgets {2,5,10} and a frozen shifted schedule doubling one measurement type’s cost.
falsifier: No operational top-k superiority if the paired accuracy-area interval fails to exceed the prespecified meaningful gain of 0.02. Apply the same criterion separately to Pareto. Neither failure disproves the broader archive concept.
